request: Add a 1.5 millimetre rib to increase support and make the structure strong.

actions.target: Add a new longitudinal reinforcing rib inside the underside mass-relief cavity, joining the cavity roof and surrounding load-bearing web to the mounting-base region without obstructing the clevis gap, pin bore, or four mounting holes.
actions.relational_constraint: The rib must be integral with the existing load-bearing web and mounting base. Locate it within the open underside relief, orient its principal span along the clevis-to-base load path, and terminate it at or above the principal underside mounting plane so that it does not protrude below FACE 77. Preserve the four mounting bores and the raised clevis interface.
actions.unresolved_reference: The request does not explicitly specify the rib location, extent, or orientation. Localization is inferred from the strengthening intention: the underside mass-relief cavity is the available low-mass region where an added rib can most directly reinforce F005 between the clevis-supporting body and R01. Final rib endpoints must be trimmed to the actual cavity boundaries after interrogating the B-rep.
steps: Localize the edit in R02, the load-bearing web and relieved body. Use F006 as the placement region and F005 as the structural feature to be reinforced. Treat FACE 92 as the principal upper boundary or roof of the underside relief; FACE 57, FACE 66, FACE 95, FACE 100, and FACE 107 define candidate cavity walls to which the rib may terminate.

Use FACE 77 of F009 as the mounting-plane datum and lower envelope. The new rib must not extend below this y=-0.010000 mm plane. Preserve FACE 77 as the installed seating interface except where a flush, coplanar rib termination is intentionally united with the base.

Establish a longitudinal construction plane through the useful central portion of the underside cavity. Orient this plane to follow the primary load path from the web beneath R03 toward R01. Based on the model coordinates and views, the rib should run generally along CAD X while its specified 1.5 mm thickness is developed generally across CAD Z.

Position the construction plane within the widest unobstructed part of F006. Confirm from the -Y and isometric geometry that the selected plane does not intersect the four mounting-hole walls FACE 49, FACE 50, FACE 51, or FACE 52 and does not enter the raised clevis gap bounded by FACE 90 and FACE 89.

Project or intersect the cavity boundaries onto the construction plane. Use the intersection with FACE 92 to define the rib's upper attachment and use the applicable cavity end walls from FACE 57, FACE 66, FACE 95, FACE 100, and FACE 107 to establish connected rib endpoints.

Sketch a closed rib profile on the construction plane. Extend the profile from the cavity roof down toward the mounting-base region, keeping its lower boundary coincident with or slightly above the FACE 77 datum. Shape the rib as a tapered or triangular web where appropriate so that it follows the existing inclined load path rather than creating an unsupported rectangular plate.

Ensure that the sketch overlaps the existing solid at the roof and at its end or base attachments. Avoid isolated contact at a single edge or point; provide finite-area intersections with F005 and R01 so the subsequent union produces one continuous solid.

Create the rib using a symmetric extrusion normal to the sketch plane with an overall thickness of exactly 1.5 mm. If a native rib operation is available, use a centered 1.5 mm rib feature with extension set to the next encountered cavity faces. Otherwise, extrude the closed profile 0.75 mm to each side.

Trim or limit the extrusion by the surrounding F006 cavity faces so that the rib remains internal to the relieved body. Boolean-union the rib with SOLID 0 and verify that it merges with the structural web at FACE 92 and with the mounting-base or cavity-wall regions at its lower and longitudinal ends.

Where manufacturing and available space permit, add tangent root blends at the rib-to-web and rib-to-base junctions to reduce stress concentration. Keep any blend small enough that it does not break through the cavity walls, mounting holes, principal mounting plane, or clevis interface; do not alter the required 1.5 mm nominal rib thickness away from the blends.
Validate that R03 remains functionally unchanged: preserve the clevis ear side faces FACE 78, FACE 90, FACE 89, and FACE 79, and preserve the coaxial pin-bore walls FACE 44 and FACE 46.
Validate that R01 remains mountable: preserve all four mounting bores and their annular seats, and confirm that no new material protrudes below FACE 77 or blocks the fastener paths.

Inspect the completed union for a single watertight solid, adequate rib-to-parent overlap, no self-intersections, and no thin residual slivers along the curved cavity wall FACE 107. Confirm the finished rib measures 1.5 mm across its normal direction.
